findings.title: Options objects now enable rejectOnClear by default
findings.cause: The options-object destructuring uses `rejectOnClear = true`, overriding the top-level `let rejectOnClear = false` whenever callers pass `{concurrency}` without an explicit `rejectOnClear`.
findings.impact: Callers following the documented default can get unexpected `AbortError` rejections from queued tasks when `clearQueue()` is called. This is especially hazardous with `Promise.all`, where a queue teardown that used to leave pending promises discarded now rejects the aggregate.
findings.evidence: index.js:4 initializes `rejectOnClear` to false, but index.js:7 changes the omitted option default to true. readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 document `rejectOnClear` as an optional boolean with default false. The focused probe with `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` queued a pending task, called `clearQueue()`, and observed `{state:"rejected", name:"AbortError"}`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run a probe that creates `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); const pending = limit(() => 'x'); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue();` while one task is active. The pending promise rejects with `AbortError`; under the documented default it should not reject unless `rejectOnClear: true` was supplied.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: The validation guard is `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`, so only truthy non-booleans throw. Falsy invalid values such as `0`, `''`, and `null` are silently accepted.
findings.impact: The runtime accepts values outside the documented and typed API contract, making invalid configuration look valid and producing behavior that depends on JavaScript truthiness rather than a boolean option.
findings.evidence: index.js:12 contains the truthiness-gated type check. readme.md:46-49 and index.d.ts:99-106 specify a boolean option. The focused probe observed `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})`, `rejectOnClear: ''`, and `rejectOnClear: null` all being accepted.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Assert that `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})` and `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: null})` throw `TypeError`. They currently do not.

findings.title: limitFunction drops every caller argument
findings.cause: `limitFunction` returns a zero-argument wrapper and invokes `function_()` instead of forwarding `...arguments_` into the wrapped function.
findings.impact: Any reusable limited function that expects parameters receives `undefined` for them. This breaks the exported TypeScript contract and documented recipes such as `limitedFetchUrl(url)`.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-124 returns `() => limit(() => function_())`. index.d.ts:133-136 declares that the returned function accepts the same arguments as `function_`; index.test-d.ts:24-26 type-checks `lf('input')`; recipes.md:161-163 demonstrates passing `url` into a limited function. The focused probe `limitFunction(async (a, b) => [a, b], {concurrency: 1})('left', 'right')` returned `[undefined, undefined]` (serialized as `[null,null]`).
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add a runtime test: `const limited = limitFunction(async (a, b) => [a, b], {concurrency: 1}); t.deepEqual(await limited('left', 'right'), ['left', 'right']);` It currently returns `[undefined, undefined]`.

findings.title: limit.map with non-array iterables no longer passes indexes
findings.cause: The mapper call passes `index` only when `Array.isArray(iterable)` is true, and passes `undefined` for Sets, generators, and other iterable inputs.
findings.impact: The documented `limit.map(iterable, mapperFunction)` contract says the mapper receives value and index for any iterable. Consumers using a Set or iterator and relying on the index now get `undefined`, causing wrong results such as `NaN`, duplicate keys, or misplaced output metadata.
findings.evidence: index.js:107-112 computes `iterableIsArray` and passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`. readme.md:78-85 says the mapper receives item value and index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`; index.d.ts:40-43 types `index` as `number`. Existing tests at test.js:239-254 cover Set and array-iterator inputs but do not assert the index. The focused probe `limit.map(new Set(['a','b','c']), (_value, index) => index)` returned `[undefined, undefined, undefined]` (serialized as `[null,null,null]`).
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add a runtime test: `const result = await limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (_value, index) => index); t.deepEqual(result, [0, 1]);` It currently returns `[undefined, undefined]`.

findings.title: Infinity concurrency support was removed
findings.cause: `validateConcurrency` now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency) && concurrency > 0` and no longer allows `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`.
findings.impact: Callers that use `pLimit(Infinity)` or set `limit.concurrency = Infinity` to disable limiting now get a `TypeError`, even though the prior implementation explicitly supported that sentinel.
findings.evidence: The local diff for index.js shows the previous guard allowed `(Number.isInteger(concurrency) || concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) && concurrency > 0`; current index.js:127-129 rejects Infinity. The focused probe `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` returned `{accepted:false, name:"TypeError", message:"Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up"}`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add a regression test that `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY).concurrency` is `Infinity` and that assigning `limit.concurrency = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` does not throw. Both paths currently throw.
